full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam, J: This Rule arises out of an application filed under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against the order No. 15 dated 22-2-95 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 54 of 1985 by the learned District Judge, Jhenidah allowing an application for addition of parties. 

 2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 16 of 1081 for declaration that the petitioner is the successor of the defunct Bainchitola Islamia Junior Madrasha and for declaration of Title to the Suit land appended to the plaint, in the court of the Subordinate Judge, Jessore which was registered as Title Suit No. 26 of 1979 and subsequently after the establishment of the subordinate Judge's court at Jhenidah it was transferred to the new court and renumbered as Title Suit No. 16 of 1981. In that suit one Badaruddin was made defendant No. 7 and the summons of the suit was served on the defendants in due course and thereafter the suit was decreed ex parte by the Judgment and decree dated 20-11-82. After passing of the aforesaid ex parte decree the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 namely, one Harun Ali and Badaruddin filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 76 of 1982. That Miscellaneous Case was resisted by the present petitioner by filing a written objection wherein have asserted that the summons of the suit was duly served on the defendants and the learned trial Court after recording evidence and hearing die parties dismissed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No.76 of 1982 vide its Judgment and order dated 23-4-85 and being aggrieved by the aforesaid Judgment and order dated 23-4-85 the defendant No. 7 Badaruddin preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 54 of 1985 before the learned District Judge. During the pendency of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal one Khondoker Moulana Mesbahul Alam Azad Khandani filed an application under Order 1 rule 10 of the case claiming himself as Secretary of Bainchitala Islamia Junior Madrasha, for adding him as appellant in the aforesaid appeal, That application was allowed by the appellate Court and against the order the petitioner preferred a revisional application before the High Court Division Which was registered as Civil Revision No. 216 of 1985 in the then Jessore Bench of the High Court Division and ultimately, it was re-numbered as Civil Revision 3602 of 1991(Dhaka). A Single Bench of this High Court Division by its order dated 2-8-94 made the Rule absolute ex parte after hearing the petitioner as none entered appearance on behalf of the opposite party. During the pendency of the Civil Revision before this court Badaruddin died on 22-12-92. After the disposal of the aforesaid Civil Revision the record of the Lower Court was sent to the appellate Court below and the record was shown to the learned Advocate for the defendant appellant on 8-1-95Thereafter on 22-1-95 the heirs of said. Badaruddin filed an application under Order 1 rule 10 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for adding them as appellants in place of Badaruddin as his heirs. In that application they stand that although the record of the case was shown to the learned. Advocate on 8-1-95 but the learned Advocate did not make any correspondence with the opposite parties and they came to know about the abatement of the appeal from the secretary of the petitioner and as such they filed the application for adding them as appellants on 22-2-95. It appears from the record that none was found to move that application and the learned appellate Court below on consideration of the contents of the application allowed the same and added the opposite parties as appellants under they Order 1 rule 10 of the Code by the impugned order dated 22-2-95. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order the petitioners preferred this revisional application to call in question the legality and propriety of the aforesaid order passed by learned appellate Court below and obtained the instant Rule. 

 3. Mr. HN Nandi, the learned Advocate appearing (or the plaintiff-petitioner, submits that the learned appellate Court below committed an error of law In allowing the application filed by the opposite parties in view of the facts that the petitioners did not assert in their application under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code that they have inherited the said suit property as heir of their deceased father defendant No.7 Badaruddin. The learned Advocate further submits that in their application, on the other hand, they asserted that they wanted to be added as appellants to protect the interest of their deceased father and at the same time they asserted that their father was Borgadar of the suit land under the Bainchitala Junior Madrasha and after his death they have taken Borga of the suit land from the said Madrasha. These assertions are contradictory and conflict with one another. The learned Advocate further submits that in view of the fact that the opposite parties have failed to show that they have succeeded to the Estate of their deceased father, they can neither be added as appellants under the provisions of Order I rule 10 nor under Order 22 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure because in both the cases, it is the requirement of law that they must show that they have succeeded to the estate left by their deceased father. The learned Advocate further submits that the petitioner has made Badaruddin and others defendants in the interest of justice and for greater interest of the plaintiff-petitioners and.in the application filed under Order 9 rule 13 deceased Badaruddin himself asserted that he was simply entrusted by the Bainchitala Junior Madrasha to manage the property and there is nothing on record to show that, that right of management has devolved upon the opposite parties on the death of said Badaruddin. In this connection he refers to the decision reported in PW 1974 (Lahore) 312. 

 4. Mr A Salam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the added opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that there is no dispute between the parties that the opposite parties are heirs of deceased defendant Badaruddin and since Badaruddin was defendant No.7 in the suit the opposite parties as heirs of Badaruddin are, as of right, entitled to be added as appellants in the aforesaid miscellaneous appeal under the provisions of Order I rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in that view of the matter the appellate Court below rightly relying on the decision reported in 22 DLR 500 and 42 DLR 481 has allowed the application. The learned Advocate further submits that misquoting of section cannot stand in the way of a party to get the desired relief. In the instant case although the application was filed under Order I rule 10 of the Code but, in fact they were substituted in place of deceased defendant appellant by virtue of the provisions of Order XXII rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate relying on the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD) 96, further submits that it is now well settled that on setting aside the order of the lower appellate Court by High Court Division, the appeal before the learned appellate Court became pending and after arrival of the records an opportunity for substitution of the heirs of the deceased appellant is available to the party concerned and, in that view of the matter, the appellate Court below rightly substituted the opposite parties as heirs of deceased defendant appellant. The learned Advocate also relies on 22 DLR 500 and submits that in the interest of justice in the instant case the heirs of the deceased appellant can be added as parties in the instant miscellaneous appeal. 

 5. On a perusal of the impugned order it appears that the appellate Court below relying on the decision reported in 22 DLR 500 and 41 DLR 481 has allowed the application filed by the opposite parties under Order I rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that it is an appropriate case where they are entitled to be added as parties. 

 6. I have gone through the decisions reported in 22 DLR 500 as well as the decision reported in 41 DLR 481 and the facts of those cases are quite distinguishable from the facts of the instant case. In both the cases the heirs of the deceased plaintiff appellant after the abatement of the appeal filed application for adding them as parties and it-has been held that in an appropriate case even if a suit is abated, the heirs of deceased party can be allowed to be added as party, and in both the cases there in no dispute that the heirs of the deceased inherited the Estate left by the deceased plaintiff, but in the instant case it was asserted by the deceased defendant appellant Badaruddin that he was entrusted by the Bainchitala Junior Madrasha to manage the suit property. Even if this statement is hundred percent correct then also on his death the right to manage the suit property does not devolve upon the heirs of deceased Badaruddin in the absence of any positive assertion to the effect that they have been entrusted by the said Madrasha to manage the property on the death of Badaruddin, The right which deceased Badruddin had was a personal right conferred on him by the Bainchitala Junior Madrasha. In the instant case there is no evidence nor there is any assertion made by the opposite parties that after the death of their father they have been entrusted by the said Madrasha to manage the suit property In this connection it may be mentioned that in connection with the aforesaid miscellaneous application Khondoker Moulana Mesbahul Alam Azad Khandani claiming himself as Secretary of the Bainchitala Junior Madrasha tried to implead himself as appellant in the aforesaid miscellaneous appeal and that application for adding him as appellant. was allowed by the appellate Court below but against that order a revisional application was preferred by the plaintiff petitioner before this court which was registered as Civil Revision No. 3602 of 1991 and the Rule in that revisional application was made absolute on finding that the said Badaruddin is not the owner of the suit property and against that ,order an appeal was preferred before the Appellate Division which was dismissed and that the alleged dispute between Bainchitala Junior Madrasha and the plaintiff petitioners attained its finality. In the application filed under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure the opposite parties have now come up with a plea that their father was a Borgadar of the suit land under the aforesaid madrasha and after his death they have taken Barga of the suit land from the said Madrasha. I have already pointed out that Badaruddin himself did not claim to be a Borgadar under the said Madrasha in his application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code but his heirs for the first time have come up with an application under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code stating that their father was a Borgadar under the Bainchitala Madrasha and on his death they have taken Borga settlement of the suit land from the aforesaid Madrsha. It is alleged that on the death of their father they have taken Borga of the suit land from the said Madrasha and even if it be a fact then also they cannot be added as parties in the instant suit because they have no independent right to call in question the legality and propriety of the decree passed in Title suit No. 16 of 1991 wherein they were not parties. 

 7. Be it an application under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code or an application for substitution under Order 22 rule 4 of the Code the opposite parties must show that they have inherited the Estate left by their deceased father but it is clear from the assertion made by both deceased Badaruddin in his application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the present opposite parties in their application under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code that no Estate has been left by their father to which they have succeeded on his death. Thus they do not come within the ambit of legal representative as contemplated in rule 4 of Order 22 of the Code. In the case reported in PLD 1974 (Lah) 312, it has been held that the successors of a deceased do not become legal representative within the meaning of rule 4 of Order 22 of the Code if no Estate is left by the deceased to be succeeded by the successors. In the instant case admittedly the suit property is not the personal property of deceased Badaruddin and it did never belong to him. So, no question of inheritance does arise in respect of the suit land by the opposite parties as heirs of deceased Badaruddin. In that view of the matter the application filed by them can neither be allowed under Order I rule 10 or under Order 22 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the learned Appellate court below misdirecting himself and on a total misconception of law and facts erroneously allowed the application filed by the opposite parties for adding them as appellants in the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 54 of 1985. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute with a cost of Taka 2,000.00 (two thousand). The Judgment and order No. 25 dated 22-2-95 passed by the learned District Judge, Jhenidah in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 54 of 1995 is set aside and the application dated 22-2-95 filed by the opposite parties is rejected.
